incidents.title: Scammers use AI to impersonate immigration attorneys to dupe immigrants with fake legal services
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Angel Leal, a South Florida immigration attorney with over 30 years of experience, has become the victim of an extensive AI-powered identity theft scheme targeting vulnerable immigrants. Criminals have created hundreds of fake social media profiles and AI-generated videos using Leal's likeness to promote fraudulent immigration services, including false promises of US residency for $2,200 payments. The scam escalated dramatically over the past three months, with scammers directing victims through WhatsApp to exchange phony contracts and collect money via Venmo, Zelle, and Cash App.

After discovering the fraud when potential clients called his office, Leal hired an anti-piracy company that has removed nearly 6,500 fake profiles, including 3,500 from TikTok, 2,400 from Facebook, and 544 from Instagram. The videos falsely feature supposed former clients praising Leal's services and claim he can secure the release of detainees for specific fees. Leal has changed his personal phone number and plans to contact local and federal authorities this week to launch an investigation into the scams' origin.

incidents.title: ASIC warns scammers are using AI to spin vast webs of deception
incidents.summary:
A fabricated article featuring ABC finance presenter Alan Kohler and Reserve Bank governor Michele Bullock in a heated interview is among a growing wave of investment scams using artificial intelligence. The fake piece promoted Boulder Sparhaven, an unlicensed cryptocurrency trading platform, by claiming Bullock stormed out over Kohler's questions about it. The Australian Securities and Investments Commission reports that AI-generated deepfakes of celebrities and politicians are becoming increasingly common and convincing, making these schemes harder to detect.

ASIC removed 19,400 scams last year, a 182 percent increase, including 7,051 fake investment platforms and 5,476 phishing scams. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese tops the list of impersonated figures, alongside Opposition Leader Angus Taylor, Pauline Hanson, and others including businessman Dick Smith and billionaire Gina Rinehart. Scammers now create elaborate webs of deception using fake news articles, websites, and advertisements. ASIC advises consumers to verify Australian Financial Services license numbers through its public registers and warns that small initial payments may be used to build trust before larger fraud occurs.

incidents.title: Sleep Staging Is Not Guesswork
incidents.summary:
A class-action lawsuit has been filed against Oura, the smart ring company valued at approximately 11 billion dollars, for allegedly making false claims about its sleep tracking capabilities. The lawsuit, filed by Clarkson Law Firm in San Francisco, accuses Oura of deceiving consumers by marketing rings priced at 300 dollars and higher as capable of detecting sleep stages with the same accuracy as hospital sleep labs. The suit claims that Oura's algorithms and sensors cannot accurately measure different sleep stages and that the company's advertised 95 percent accuracy compared to clinical sleep labs is misleading, since Oura devices lack the complex equipment required for genuine medical-grade sleep analysis.

Oura has responded by defending its technology, stating that its rings use multiple physiological signals including heart rate and temperature to estimate sleep stages and that independent studies support its accuracy claims. The company emphasizes that its products are consumer devices, not medical equipment. Experts note that like other health trackers, Oura rings provide estimates rather than precise measurements and should not be overemphasized as diagnostic tools. It remains unclear what compensation customers might receive if the lawsuit succeeds, and this is not Oura's first legal challenge, as another class-action suit alleges the company collected personal data without consent.

incidents.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that the Aurora ransomware group, active since April 2026, has developed a Linux variant targeting ESXi virtual environments. The group used Cursor Agent, running Claude Sonnet AI, to conduct hands-on attacks against ten organizations between April and May 2026. The ESXi ransomware encrypts virtual machine files using ChaCha20 encryption while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see ransom demands. A custom tool called esxi_finder.py helps attackers locate ESXi hosts and vCenter servers within victim networks by scanning ports and reading TLS certificates.

Researchers also identified a second Aurora operator cluster with medium confidence, affecting eight victim organizations across multiple countries. This cluster used different tactics including SQL Server exploitation, privilege escalation, and data exfiltration to self-hosted S3 storage. The attackers imposed strict operational restrictions when using Cursor Agent, including prohibitions on using DCSync, locking accounts, or adding computer objects to domains. The investigation exposed numerous IP addresses, URLs, and file hashes associated with both clusters' command and control infrastructure and exfiltration capabilities.

incidents.title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries
incidents.summary:
A major Pizza Hut franchisee has filed a lawsuit claiming that Pizza Hut's new AI-powered delivery system called Dragontail caused over $100 million in damages to its business. Chaac Pizza Northeast, which operates approximately 111 Pizza Hut locations across the Northeast, says the system created operational problems after the 2024 rollout. The platform gave DoorDash drivers real-time visibility into kitchen operations, allowing them to see when pizzas would be ready and tip amounts, which allegedly caused drivers to wait up to fifteen minutes to batch multiple orders together, significantly delaying deliveries.

Before the system launched, Chaac says more than 90 percent of its deliveries arrived within 30 minutes and the company had double-digit sales growth. After Dragontail's implementation, delivery performance deteriorated sharply and customer satisfaction dropped. In New York City specifically, year-over-year sales growth fell from positive 10.19 percent to negative 9.78 percent. The franchisee claims Pizza Hut failed to provide adequate training or support and ignored worsening delivery metrics. Pizza Hut stated it would respond through legal channels but declined further comment. The lawsuit comes as Pizza Hut's parent company plans to close 250 US locations this year.

incidents.title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Scammers are impersonating Terry Gross and other NPR staff members to defraud people seeking media appearances. The fraudulent emails target authors, entertainers and public figures with personalized messages referencing their work and proposing interviews. Recipients are eventually asked to pay fees, typically around $250, for supposed production costs. A Misericordia University history professor became suspicious when the email appeared to come directly from Gross herself and included AI-like language, then received a payment request. Similar scams have targeted comedians and other celebrities, with some victims directed to provide social media login credentials.

WHYY, NPR and Fresh Air have confirmed they are aware of these fraudulent emails and are working with law enforcement to investigate. The organizations stated they never charge guests for interviews and that any payment requests should be considered illegitimate. Cybersecurity experts note that artificial intelligence has made impersonation scams more convincing and personalized than traditional mass fraud attempts. They recommend verifying interview invitations directly with the organization through legitimate contact information rather than responding to suspicious emails.

incidents.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
incidents.summary:
# Summary

An Israeli-funded fake think tank called the Hanover Institute published over 560,000 words across 124 reports in just nine days using a platform designed to optimize content for artificial intelligence systems like ChatGPT. The nonexistent institute, which has no physical address or named staff, presented pro-Israel arguments on contentious topics including alleged war crimes, genocide claims, and Palestinian casualties. A New York media company called Piro Inc disclosed the operation to the US Justice Department under foreign agent registration laws, revealing it was part of a broader Israeli government campaign financed through tens of millions of dollars routed via European advertising firm Havas Media.

The campaign aimed to influence how chatbots present Israeli positions by seeding websites into training data used by AI systems. Israeli officials have expressed doubts about the effort's effectiveness, with some calling it a waste of government money as American public support for Israel has declined significantly. Researchers noted that while the operation successfully shapes chatbot responses, it fails to change public opinion polling, which remains the Israeli government's actual concern. The broader campaign represents a new form of information manipulation where foreign governments and companies attempt to poison AI training data to influence automated responses.

incidents.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
incidents.summary:
Major record labels, including Universal Music Group, Sony Music, Warner Music, Capitol Records, and Atlantic Records, have filed separate lawsuits against Udio and Suno, two popular AI music generators. The labels accuse both companies of scraping massive amounts of copyrighted music without permission to train their AI models and of directly reproducing sections of famous songs in their generated content. The lawsuits claim the companies have been deliberately hiding what music they used for training, despite claiming in earlier communications that their activities constitute fair use.

To demonstrate their claims, the record labels created AI-generated songs using specific prompts and compared them to copyrighted works they hold rights to, submitting thousands of examples as evidence. The labels documented instances where the AI reproduced distinctive elements of songs by artists including The Beatles, Chuck Berry, Green Day, Mariah Carey, and many others. One example showed an Udio-generated song copying the entire first verse lyrics of Green Day's American Idiot, while another Suno output nearly replicated Mariah Carey's All I Want for Christmas Is You. The lawsuits represent a major court battle over how generative AI companies train their models using copyrighted material.

Universal Music Group has settled a lawsuit against AI music startup Udio, which was accused of using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence system. The case involved allegations that Udio generated music similar to existing hits, including The Temptations' "My Girl." Under the new licensing agreements, Udio will launch a platform next year trained exclusively on authorized and licensed music, allowing users to create, customize, and share songs while compensating artists and songwriters involved.

This settlement represents Udio's first major licensing deal with a major music label and signals a shift toward cooperation between AI companies and the entertainment industry. Udio's CEO stated the partnership would unite AI and the music industry while supporting artists. The startup, launched in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees and backed by investors including will.i.am, has attracted millions of users since its release. UMG did not disclose financial terms of the agreement and simultaneously announced a separate partnership with Stability AI to develop music creation tools for artists and producers.

incidents.title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings
incidents.summary:
State Farm's defense lawyers in a Los Angeles lawsuit have admitted to using artificial intelligence that generated false legal cases, quotes, and rulings in court filings. The homeowner's attorney discovered seven nonexistent case citations across eight filings, along with incorrect case titles and fabricated quotes. The lawsuit involves Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga, whose home in Carson became uninhabitable after a 2020 fire. While repairs were underway, storm damage occurred, and State Farm allegedly delayed approvals, leaving the home unfinished. Meni-Siliga and her husband exhausted their savings, filed for bankruptcy, and lost the home to foreclosure.

One State Farm lawyer, Jacquelene Robinson, explained she used an AI tool called Irys, mistakenly believing it was connected to her law firm's legal research subscription with built-in accuracy checks. Lead counsel Kenneth Katel apologized to the court and the plaintiff, accepting responsibility despite claiming he was unaware AI had been used. The case is scheduled for trial in October. The incident reflects a growing trend, with 41 percent of law firms and 47 percent of corporate legal departments now using generative AI, raising concerns about accuracy in legal filings.

stories.Headline: Roundup: Chinese AI gaining popularity in Kenya for affordability, performance, customization
stories.Summary:
Chinese artificial intelligence models are becoming increasingly popular among Kenyan developers and technology companies due to their affordability, strong performance, and customizable open-source design. According to recent data, Chinese AI models represented roughly half of AI use on OpenRouter, up from less than 25 percent a year prior, and accounted for 19 of the 25 most-downloaded open-source systems on Hugging Face. Kenyan companies are adopting Chinese models like DeepSeek and Qwen for applications including legal technology, business intelligence, and document processing.

Local technology leaders highlight that Chinese models consume fewer computing resources than Western alternatives while delivering comparable or superior performance, making them practical for Kenya's limited GPU supply. The open-weight nature of these models allows developers to customize them for local languages and African-specific needs without building systems from scratch. Companies like JibuDocs and Qhala are already leveraging these models for innovative applications, while experts suggest potential uses in healthcare diagnostics and disaster prevention could serve underserved African communities.

stories.Headline: Oklahoma State University adds new AI, logistics programs for fall semester
stories.Summary:
Oklahoma State University Institute of Technology is launching two new academic programs beginning in fall 2026. The first is a 60-credit-hour online Associate in Applied Science in Logistics and Supply Chain Technology that students can complete in four to five semesters. This program covers warehousing, transportation, inventory management, and data-informed decision-making, preparing graduates for careers as logistics coordinators, distribution center managers, inventory specialists, and supply chain coordinators. The second offering is an Applied Artificial Intelligence option within the existing Bachelor of Technology in Information Technologies program.

The university designed both programs to address workforce demands in Oklahoma and beyond. The logistics program prepares students for industry-recognized credentials that can lead to over 11 million jobs nationwide. The artificial intelligence program goes beyond teaching tool usage, instead focusing on applying AI technologies to solve real organizational problems while considering ethics and governance. OSUIT Provost Dr. Richie Roberts stated that preparing students with skills aligned to industry needs helps build a strong workforce supporting the state's economic growth.

stories.Headline: What We Know About Haryana Police's AI Task Force.
stories.Summary:
Haryana Police is establishing an Artificial Intelligence Task Force to expand AI use in law enforcement operations. An Indian Police Service officer will lead the initiative, which focuses on cybercrime investigations, financial transaction analysis, complaint management and court information processing. The police emphasized that AI will support human investigators rather than replace them, with officers responsible for verifying leads and making final decisions.

The task force will build on existing technology systems Haryana Police already uses, including a 2022 facial recognition program that deactivated nearly 1,000 fraudulent SIM cards and current cybercrime helplines. The police plan to implement safeguards around accuracy, transparency, data security and human oversight, though specific implementation details remain unclear. Haryana Police has not disclosed how it will test systems, measure errors, conduct audits or handle incorrect results, and has not explained how new AI capabilities will integrate with current infrastructure or whether it plans to use facial recognition or predictive policing technologies.

stories.Headline: EU places ChatGPT, Reddit, Roblox under strictest platform rules
stories.Summary:
The European Union has classified ChatGPT as a Very Large Online Search Engine and designated Reddit and Roblox as Very Large Online Platforms under its Digital Services Act. These three American companies will now face direct supervision from the European Commission and must comply with stricter requirements designed to address risks related to children, election integrity, and public security. The rules apply to services with over 45 million users in the EU, bringing the total number of regulated platforms to 28.

Companies failing to meet the new requirements within four months face fines up to 6 percent of their annual global revenue. Reddit reported 57.2 million EU users in July, while Roblox has 46.6 million. OpenAI stated it would prepare to meet ChatGPT's additional obligations, and Roblox welcomed the designation, emphasizing safety's importance. This designation adds another regulatory layer for ChatGPT, which already complies with the EU's Artificial Intelligence Act.

stories.Headline: 《TAIPEI TIMES》 Taiwan aims to train 500,000 AI pros by 2040 - 焦點
stories.Summary:
Taiwan's government plans to invest over 40 billion Taiwan dollars, approximately 1.26 billion US dollars, to develop 10 major artificial intelligence projects next year. President William Lai has set an ambitious goal to train at least 500,000 AI professionals by 2040. The administration launched the AI Talent Ark Project this year to nurture talent through fundamental education, professional development, and data-driven approaches, aiming to build a large AI talent pool and strengthen Taiwan's competitiveness in technology sectors.

The government is also prioritizing technological sovereignty and national resilience. The Minister of Digital Affairs announced plans to accumulate at least 10,000 graphics processing units through private investment in AI computing centers within a year. Taiwan is focusing on developing sovereign AI systems that understand Taiwanese perspectives and languages, along with low-Earth-orbit satellite communications to ensure independent communication capabilities. Officials emphasized that technological sovereignty means focusing on critical technologies rather than developing every technology domestically.

stories.Headline: CSA's Top Cloud Threats: Identity, AI -- Campus Technology
stories.Summary:
The Cloud Security Alliance surveyed 507 security professionals to identify the top threats to cloud computing in 2026. Identity and access management issues rose to the number one concern, moving up from second place in 2024, while misconfiguration dropped to fifth. Two artificial intelligence-related threats appeared in the rankings for the first time, including AI-enhanced attacks and AI system compromise. The top eleven threats also include insecure third-party resources, insecure APIs, advanced persistent threats, and inadequate cloud security strategy and governance.

The survey results reveal a significant shift in the cloud threat landscape, with organizations now prioritizing identity protection, artificial intelligence risks, and software supply chains over infrastructure-focused concerns. Security scores ranged closely from 7.95 for identity and access management to 7.45 for system vulnerabilities. The report aims to help organizations make informed risk-management decisions about cloud adoption by providing expert analysis of technical and business impacts, real-world examples, and corresponding security controls across cloud and AI environments.

stories.Headline: Who Writes AI's Rules When Someone Else Owns the Machines?
stories.Summary:
# Summary

South Africa withdrew its Draft National AI Policy in April 2026 after discovering that at least six of its 67 academic references were fabricated, highlighting a broader challenge facing the Global South. The incident underscores a critical debate about who controls artificial intelligence governance and infrastructure. Currently, the United States and China host roughly 86% of global data centre capacity, giving them power to set rules and prices for AI systems worldwide. This concentration of computing power represents what critics call "tech colonialism," where developing nations provide data and demand but lack ownership and control over the technology itself.

BRICS countries and other Global South nations are attempting to shift AI governance away from Western-led standards by emphasizing digital sovereignty and development rights. They are seeking to anchor AI governance within the United Nations rather than OECD-led bodies and have established organizations like the World Artificial Intelligence Cooperation Organisation. However, meaningful sovereignty requires owning physical infrastructure, not just adopting policies. The article notes that until developing nations build regional computing capacity and chip manufacturing capabilities, they remain dependent on foreign platforms controlled by American hyperscalers or Chinese firms. True sovereignty means choosing dependencies rather than having them imposed.

India is hosting its first dedicated summit focused on artificial intelligence in marketing in September 2026. The AIM Summit will take place on September 17 in Bengaluru and September 18 in New Delhi, bringing together over 50 chief marketing officers from major brands including Paytm, KFC, Nestle, and Uniqlo. The event expects to attract more than 600 marketing professionals as attendees and delegates.

The summit aims to move beyond theoretical discussions about artificial intelligence and instead focus on practical implementation and real-world applications. The program will include an AI Lab for hands-on exploration of technology capabilities, an exhibition showcasing marketing solution providers, and an awards ceremony recognizing innovative organizations. Sessions will cover topics such as content creation, personalization, customer experience, marketing automation, and analytics. The summit is being organized with CXO Lanes, a community of over 500,000 executives across India.

stories.Headline: AI Now Writes 86% of Paisabazaar's New Code, Reshaping How its Engineers Build Productively and Innovatively
stories.Summary:
Paisabazaar, India's leading financial products marketplace, reports that artificial intelligence now generates approximately 86 percent of new code written on its platform. The company's Chief Technology Officer emphasized that the objective is not to eliminate engineers but to enhance their productivity by automating repetitive tasks. This shift allows engineers to focus on architecture, problem-solving and innovation while accelerating development velocity and enabling teams to pursue a larger product roadmap.

The financial services company is expanding its engineering team despite increased AI involvement, demonstrating its commitment to using productivity gains for expansion rather than workforce reduction. AI-assisted development is integrated throughout the engineering lifecycle, including code writing, testing, debugging and documentation. The company plans to continue deepening AI adoption across both engineering and consumer-facing experiences to expand innovation, improve productivity and deliver more personalized financial services at scale.

stories.Headline: Dyna.Ai Selected as Technology Partner in Hong Kong's GenA.I. Sandbox++
stories.Summary:
Dyna.Ai, a Singapore-based AI company, has been selected as a technology partner in Hong Kong's new GenA.I. Sandbox++ program, marking its second consecutive selection by Hong Kong financial regulators. The sandbox was jointly launched by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, Securities and Futures Commission, Insurance Authority, and Mandatory Provident Fund Schemes Authority in collaboration with Cyberport. Out of nearly 100 regional proposals, 36 use cases involving 30 financial institutions and 27 technology providers were chosen, including major institutions like Bank of China (Hong Kong) and Manulife (International), alongside technology partners Google, IBM, and Dyna.Ai.

Unlike earlier programs focused on generative AI banking pilots, Sandbox++ expands across banking, insurance, securities, and pension funds to test Agentic AI systems that execute complex tasks under real-time governance. Dyna.Ai will demonstrate how financial institutions can safely delegate workflow execution to autonomous AI agents while maintaining strict oversight and compliance. The company plans to showcase its solutions and governance frameworks at LEAP 2026 in Riyadh later this year.
